partialCapture.note:
Neither the 456-frame sweep nor the 12-theme sweep was regenerated. Frames added or refreshed here were captured against the same guards (assertFramePaints) but only in the two brand themes, and the live-app frames came from the real Electron window rather than Storybook. The spacing round REFRESHED the five chat-tool-rows surfaces because the row pitch changed under them, and added two: `spacing-uniformity` reproduces the three runs the operator screenshotted, `turn-boundary` shows the hierarchy that survives the tightening. `narrow` and `working-labels` are now captured in a viewport sized to their content — at 1280x900 they were mostly empty ground and crossed the uniformity ceiling once the rows tightened. REMEDIATION ROUND 1: all seven chat-tool-rows surfaces were refreshed again, because the name/summary gutter, the running row's live clock, the sr-only outcome text and the summary fallback all changed what they show. REMEDIATION ROUND 2: `real-conversation-tool-rows` was RE-CAPTURED and is no longer stale. It now shows 38 real tool rows with 0 blank object columns on a 20px pitch, rendered by the shipped reducer and the shipped CanonicalTranscript over real /history pages paged oldest-first in 20-entry pages (the cross-page condition the blank-summary defect needed). Electron is not required for this surface — the desktop API answers a plain bearer request. The reading was proven falsifiable by running the SAME harness with the reducer starved: stripping tool_calls alone still yields 0 blanks (the output fallback carries it), stripping tool_calls AND output yields 53 of 53 blank, reproducing the original defect from the current head. DIFF BODY: two surfaces were ADDED — the `write`/`edit` row's expansion now paints the result's own unified diff instead of its arguments JSON — and four frames were taken for them in the two brand palettes (`chat-tool-rows--diff-body` at 1280x2110 and `chat-tool-rows--diff-body-narrow` at 560x1380). The four Storybook frames are committed under `write-edit-diff/` rather than under the story-id directory the capturer derives (`chat-tool-rows/<leaf>`), following the `tool-rows/` precedent, so that the frames sit beside the spec and README that explain them; a re-capture writes them back to `chat-tool-rows/`. `surfaces` counts the two new STORIES entries. The 12-theme sweep was NOT regenerated. A sixth frame set is declared in `supplementary` below: three real durable diff rows in one conversation (197, 58 and 14 diff lines — the first two longer than the 40-line display cap, so two overflow markers and one body shown whole) rendered by the SHIPPED reducer and transcript over real transcript.jsonl rows. The story proves the component; that one proves the wire payload reaches pixels. DIFF BODY, REMEDIATION ROUND 1: the same two Storybook surfaces were refreshed again and a THIRD was added, because the body now paints each line whole in its kind's ink instead of tinting only the leading marker (the terminal's loop is the authority; its docstring promises the other thing), and because the cap's `… N more diff lines` marker is now pinned to the well's foot with `sticky -bottom-3 pb-3 -mb-3` — it used to scroll out of view in exactly the wrapped-at-cap case it exists for. The new surface, `chat-tool-rows--diff-body-narrow-wrapped-cap` at 560x830, is the frame that shows the marker visible at rest; `frames` moves 478 -> 480 for its two palettes, and it is the only frame count that changed. The `real-durable-diff-rows` pair was RE-CAPTURED in the same round for the same reason (on the same real conversation, same three diffs of 197, 58 and 14 lines) and carries the identical marker arithmetic. It was captured from the committed source, not from a dirty tree: this partial run's `head`, `srcTree` and `scriptsTree` name the commit whose pixels these are. The neighbour `tool-rows/*` frames were NOT re-captured — they are from the August head and do not reproduce pixel-exactly on this one (a uniform 11px shift with identical internal geometry, across three stories of different content), which the write-edit-diff README records so nobody reads it as a regression from this change. DESIGN PROPOSAL ROUND: this round added a new surface, `chat-run-details` - eight story states of the run-details popover (docs/run-details.md), rendered as the REAL `ChatHeader` inside a chat-column ground with the panel open over a fixture roster and plan. Sixteen frames added (eight states x the two brand themes) and no existing frame touched, so `frames` and `surfaces` were raised by 16 and 8 rather than a sweep being run: a sweep would have rewritten 474 frames nobody reviewed to add eight that were. The frames were captured at viewports sized to each story, because a 384px popover on a 1280x900 page is more than 99% one colour and the uniformity ceiling rejects it - which is that guard working as designed. The two `settled`/`header-trigger` frames differ only in their fixture, so the presence and absence of the header button reads as one comparison. REMEDIATION: two corrections came out of reading the frames rather than out of a test. Radix's ScrollArea content wrapper is `display: table; min-width: 100%`, which sizes to max-content and silently defeats every `truncate` inside the panel - the first capture showed a long label pushing the whole numbers run past the panel's right edge. `todos-only` and `crowded` were then re-captured at 820px tall, because the panel's own `min(60vh, 480px)` ceiling is what those two frames are judged at and at a shorter viewport the item cap's `+4 more` row falls past the fold. One frame was also re-captured with `type="always"` on the ScrollArea to prove the viewport overflows and scrolls rather than being clipped by the Root (the thumb spanned 305px of the 475px viewport, so about 740px of content); the committed set is from the default `type="hover"`, which is why no still shows a scrollbar.

DESIGN REMEDIATION ROUND 1: nine findings from the design review were worked in one commit, and every one of the nine `chat-run-details` states was re-captured in the two brand themes rather than only the ones whose pixels moved - the panel's edge, its second lines and its grid all changed, and a frame that is not re-taken cannot show that. One story was ADDED, so `frames`/`surfaces` were raised by 2 and 1 by hand (a narrowed run preserves the sweep's totals, which is what `partialCapture` is for). `failure-unseen` is the regression frame for the panel unmounting while it is read: its only reason for a trigger is a failure nobody has acknowledged, and opening the panel acknowledges it in the same commit that shows it. The panel's own changes: the trigger now stays mounted while `open` (the canvas is still a hard close); the ScrollArea took `type="auto"` so an OVERFLOWING panel paints its thumb in a still - the set previously could not show the scroll state at all, because `hover` needs a pointer a capture rig does not have, and the only cue left was a row sliced by the panel's bottom edge; the popover content carries `outline-none shadow-overlay!` because it takes focus programmatically on open, so the app's unlayered `html :focus-visible` rule (a 2px accent ring plus `box-shadow: none !important`) was drawing the loudest line on the surface and suppressing the elevation the contract promises - the shadow now paints at the panel's edge in both themes; a blocked to-do's reason moved to its own indented line so neither the item nor the reason truncates to a fragment; a failed child's exception line is monospace, `ink-muted` and clamped to two lines so the identifier survives, and the activity line stays sans and single-line; the to-do grammar is `resolved` throughout (section tally and phase headers, one notion of closure) with the shed direction corrected to drop the OLDEST closed rows and the hidden rows attributed inside the phase that lost them; no row hovers, because nothing in the panel is clickable; and the two lists share one grid.

supplementary.why: The claims are a real pointer hover and a click that stages a draft. Storybook can force the revealed class but not produce the hover, and a staged draft is store state a fixture would have to fake, so these are captured from the running app against an isolated seeded backend instead. The sidebar has no story, so re-running the sweep cannot re-derive them; docs/evidence/sidebar-new-chat/README.md carries the re-capture procedure.

supplementary.source: headless Chrome over CDP, driven by `node scripts/diff-body-evidence.mjs`: the shipped `applyHistoryPage` reducer and the shipped `CanonicalTranscript` over a real durable history page read from one real session's `transcript.jsonl` in the local store (`--session` and `--anchor` are required arguments; the id is deliberately not committed)
supplementary.why: The story renders a TranscriptRecord this repository built, so it proves the component. This set starts one layer earlier, at the bytes `/v1/desktop/sessions/{id}/history` serves — the stored rows, serialised verbatim by `read_transcript_page` — and runs them through the shipped reducer, which is what proves the payload reaches pixels: the durable row's own encoding, the extraction of `provider_payload.details.diff`, the identity gate and the args-drop rule. It cannot be re-derived by the sweep, and the payload itself is deliberately NOT committed: the harness writes it to a temp file and deletes it. Re-run with `node scripts/diff-body-evidence.mjs --session=<id> --anchor=<row id>` (see docs/evidence/write-edit-diff/README.md).
